dedupe_keys.name: mine footprints in british columbia pacific salmon foundation

description: This dataset maps the footprints (areas) of mineral and aggregate mines across British Columbia. The DataCite record says the footprints were detected and delineated using Landsat image time series, provincial mining databases, a satellite-based forest inventory system, Sentinel-2 imagery and visual interpretation, and that it was made because mining affects salmon habitat through pollution, habitat loss and changes in water temperature and flow, including after closure. It was published by the Pacific Salmon Foundation as version 20240822 (2024) on its salmon watersheds data portal, free under CC BY 4.0, with provincial coverage of British Columbia. Caveats: the download format, the number of footprints and the imagery years are not stated on the pages read, and aggregate pits are mixed with metal and coal mines. For simulation it gives mapped mine disturbance areas to overlay with rivers, roads and settlements for hazard exposure and environmental impact scenarios, and to locate mines whose tailings or water releases could affect downstream water intakes. Related catalogue records include the global-scale mining polygons by Maus and others, the global high-resolution mining footprints and the tailings flows database.
